Traffic demand between chiplets

Who sends how many bytes to whom, before routing. Native replay of the oracle-best mapping on each HW (cycles equal the oracle). Updated 2026-10-21 16:38.

  • Step 1 uses only the network: which block sends data to which block. No chiplets, HW or mapping.
  • Step 2 is the same traffic after the mapping placed the layers on chiplets: which chiplet sends to which chiplet, for the uniform HW and the asymmetric HW (each with its own fastest mapping).
  • The matrices are set by the workload, the batch and the mapping. Link widths and the route change only the path. A multicast counts once per receiving chiplet.

Step 2 · Which chiplet sends to which chiplet (after mapping)

With DRAM: rows and columns include D0..D3, so a chiplet row sums to 100% over chiplets and DRAM. Chiplets only: DRAM traffic is removed before the percentages, so a row sums to 100% over the other chiplets. Cells show percent (blank below 0.5% of the sender, or below 0.05% of all bytes). With % of all bytes the shading is relative to the largest pair. Node ids: chiplets 0..N−1 (q = column × rows + row, row 0 at the top), D0..D3 = DRAM controllers. "Ring next" is the next chiplet in the ring layer-pipelining order. Parity: replay cycles equal the oracle cycles of the picked mapping on that HW.
